posts.caption:
The multitasking vitamin hiding in half your shelf 🧪
Ingredient 101 · Niacinamide (Nicotinamide (vitamin B3))
📍 Hot in Korea & abroad: #2 TikTok active (2025 study); OY searches +65%

A form of vitamin B3 that skin can use directly. It's a true multitasker: it supports the barrier, helps balance oil and helps even out the look of skin tone.

✨ What it does
• Helps even out the look of dark spots and dullness
• Supports a healthy-feeling barrier and moisture
• May help oil look balanced and pores look refined

👤 Best for: Oily or combination skin, Uneven-looking tone, Visible pores
🕐 When: AM & PM

🧴 How to use
1. Apply a serum after toner, before moisturizer
2. Start around 2–5%; go higher only if skin stays comfortable
3. Wear SPF daily for the best-looking results
🤝 Pairs well with: Vitamin C, Ceramides, Hyaluronic acid

⚠️ Good to know
• In Korea, 2–5% niacinamide can carry an official 'brightening' functional claim.
• Most products use 5% or less; a higher % isn't automatically better.
• Rarely, it may cause redness or itching, so patch test if sensitive.

❌ Myth: You can't use niacinamide with vitamin C.
✅ Fact: They can be used together, in one formula or layered, and dermatologists often pair them.

posts.caption:
The 'tiger grass' behind calm-looking K-beauty skin 🧪
Ingredient 101 · Centella (Centella asiatica (incl. madecassoside))
📍 Hot in Korea & abroad: Madecassoside pad: OY Awards 2025 winner

A leafy herb long used in Asian traditional remedies. Its key compounds (madecassoside, asiaticoside, asiatic acid and madecassic acid) are prized for calming skin.

✨ What it does
• Helps calm the look of redness and irritation
• Supports a stronger-feeling moisture barrier
• May help blemish-prone skin look more balanced

👤 Best for: Sensitive or reactive skin, Blemish-prone skin, Skin stressed by actives
🕐 When: AM & PM

🧴 How to use
1. Swipe on a centella toner or pad after cleansing
2. Follow with a centella ampoule or cream
3. Gentle enough for most skin to use twice a day
🤝 Pairs well with: Panthenol, Ceramides, Niacinamide

⚠️ Good to know
• 'Cica' is a marketing nickname; check the INCI list for centella or madecassoside.
• Much research is lab or animal-based; long-term human trials are still limited.
• Also sold as gotu kola or Indian pennywort in herbal products.

❌ Myth: Every 'cica' product is packed with centella.
✅ Fact: 'Cica' is just a nickname. Amounts vary, so look for centella or madecassoside high on the ingredient list.

posts.caption:
Salmon DNA in your serum? Here's the real story 🧪
Ingredient 101 · PDRN (Polydeoxyribonucleotide)
📍 Hot in Korea & abroad: Olive Young searches +695% YoY (Sept 2025)

PDRN is a purified blend of DNA fragments, usually from salmon. It started in clinic injections and is now one of K-beauty's most popular serum ingredients.

✨ What it does
• Helps skin feel hydrated, bouncy and comfortable
• Supports a calm, healthy-looking skin barrier
• May help skin look smoother and more radiant

👤 Best for: Dull or tired-looking skin, Dry, dehydrated skin, Early fine lines
🕐 When: AM & PM

🧴 How to use
1. Apply after toner, on slightly damp skin
2. Pat in 2–3 drops gently; no need to rub
3. Seal with moisturizer; add SPF in the morning
🤝 Pairs well with: Hyaluronic acid, Peptides, Niacinamide

⚠️ Good to know
• Most PDRN research is on injections; serum results are gentler and less studied.
• Usually salmon-derived: skip it or patch test first if you have a fish allergy.
• Labels list it as 'Sodium DNA', and some 'PDRN' is plant-derived. Check the source.

❌ Myth: A PDRN serum works like a PDRN or Rejuran injection.
✅ Fact: Injections place DNA fragments deep in skin. Serums stay near the surface: think hydration, not a procedure.

posts.caption:
Hyaluronic acid: why 'low molecular' is on the label 🧪
Ingredient 101 · Hyaluronic acid (Hyaluronic acid (sodium hyaluronate))
📍 Hot in Korea & abroad: #4 Olive Young Global skincare (Torriden, 2026)

Hyaluronic acid is a sugar-like molecule your skin already makes to hold water. Serums use it in different sizes: larger ones sit on top, smaller ones aim a little deeper.

✨ What it does
• Helps skin attract and hold surface moisture
• Supports a plumper, smoother-looking surface
• Helps skin feel comfortable right after cleansing

👤 Best for: Dehydrated skin, Tight skin after cleansing, Any skin type
🕐 When: AM & PM

🧴 How to use
1. Apply to slightly damp skin, right after toner
2. Seal it in with a moisturizer so water doesn't evaporate
3. Layer under sunscreen in the morning
🤝 Pairs well with: Ceramides, Panthenol, PDRN

⚠️ Good to know
• Human studies suggest topical HA may help hydration; results depend on the formula.
• In dry air, always top it with cream so it doesn't leave skin feeling tight.
• Labels may say sodium hyaluronate or 'low molecular' for smaller forms.

❌ Myth: More layers of hyaluronic acid mean more hydration.
✅ Fact: HA needs water around it and a cream on top. Extra layers rarely help; sealing it in does.

posts.caption:
Korea's 'scalp scaling' secret is an acne acid 💇‍♀️
Hair & scalp 101 · Salicylic acid (Salicylic acid (BHA))
📍 Hot in Korea: Key acid in Korea's 'scalp scaling' shampoos

An oil-soluble beta hydroxy acid (BHA). On the scalp it helps loosen flakes, excess oil and product buildup so they rinse away.

✨ What it does
• Helps loosen flakes and buildup around the roots
• Helps an oily scalp feel cleaner for longer
• Part of an approved hair-loss care formula in Korea

👤 Best for: Oily scalp, Flakes and buildup, Clogged-feeling scalp
🕐 When: 1–2x a week

🧴 How to use
1. Apply scaling shampoo to a wet scalp, section by section
2. Massage gently with fingertips; leave on 2–3 minutes
3. Rinse well and follow with a soothing scalp tonic
🤝 Pairs well with: Panthenol, Menthol
🚫 Don't mix with: Other exfoliants

⚠️ Good to know
• Overuse can dry or irritate the scalp. Start once a week.
• Skip it on broken, sunburned or freshly bleached skin.
• Allergic to aspirin (a salicylate)? Check with a doctor first.

❌ Myth: 'Scaling' means scrubbing your scalp hard.
✅ Fact: In Korea, 'scaling' usually means gentle chemical exfoliation with acids like BHA, not harsh scrubbing.

posts.caption:
The 'microneedle' serum that tingles, explained 🧪
Ingredient 101 · Spicules (Hydrolyzed sponge (microspicules))
📍 Hot in Korea & abroad: Reedle Shot won Olive Young Global Awards 2025

Spicules are microscopic, needle-shaped mineral bits from sea sponges. In serums they gently prickle the surface to exfoliate and help products absorb.

✨ What it does
• Gently exfoliates for smoother-feeling texture
• May help the products you apply next absorb better
• Helps skin look brighter and more refined

👤 Best for: Rough texture, visible pores, Dull skin, Healthy, non-sensitive skin
🕐 When: PM, 2–3x a week

🧴 How to use
1. Start with the lowest strength (e.g. 100) on clean, dry skin
2. Pat or massage in gently; mild tingling is normal
3. Follow with a soothing moisturizer, and SPF next day
🤝 Pairs well with: Centella (cica), Hyaluronic acid, Panthenol
🚫 Don't mix with: Retinoids same night, AHA/BHA same night

⚠️ Good to know
• Skip on broken skin, eczema, rosacea or active irritation.
• Stronger isn't better: stop if burning or redness lasts.
• Human studies are few, and overuse can weaken the skin barrier.

❌ Myth: More tingling means it's working better.
✅ Fact: Tingling is just spicules in the surface layer. Strong burning or lasting redness means back off.

posts.caption:
From rice bowl to toner: what rice does for skin 🧪
Ingredient 101 · Rice (Oryza sativa (rice) extract & ferment)
📍 Hot in Korea & abroad: I'm From Rice Toner: 3M+ sold globally by 2024

Extracts, bran water or ferments made from rice. They bring ferulic acid, gamma-oryzanol, vitamin E-family antioxidants and starches that leave skin soft and dewy.

✨ What it does
• Helps hydrate for a soft, milky-smooth feel
• Antioxidants may help defend against daily stressors
• Known for a healthy-looking, even glow

👤 Best for: Dull or uneven-looking skin, Dry to normal skin
🕐 When: AM & PM

🧴 How to use
1. Pat a milky rice toner onto skin after cleansing
2. Layer a rice serum or cream for extra softness
3. Finish with SPF in the morning (rice sunscreens exist too)
🤝 Pairs well with: Ceramides, Niacinamide, Probiotics

⚠️ Good to know
• DIY rice water isn't standardized or preserved; formulated extracts are more reliable.
• Allergic to rice or very reactive? Patch test first.
• Fermenting breaks rice into smaller compounds; most evidence is still from lab models.

❌ Myth: Homemade rice water works just like rice skincare.
✅ Fact: Kitchen rice water isn't standardized or preserved; formulated extracts and ferments are more consistent.
